learning: Iteration 3 showed that widening the sensor array to +/-0.04 m with kp 3.0 degraded every track. Iteration 1 remains the best measured layout. The next race will show whether a narrower wheel track adds turn authority without destabilising the oval. Turn gain per unit of controller output rises by about 20% with this change, so steering_oscillation is the key risk.
notes: Restores the iteration 1 sensor array and controller unchanged, and changes only wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m to test H1 (more turn authority on slalom and s-bend). Controller values are held fixed so the result can be attributed to wheel track.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 (entityR2B) is the best measured geometry. The oval finished 20 of 20 with max_error 0.025 m, the s-bend finished 8 of 20, and the slalom failed in all 20 at progress 0.18 with about 2 line-loss events. Iteration 3 widened the array to +/-0.04 m at 20 mm spacing and raised kp to 3.0. Every track degraded, and the oval fell from 20/20 finishes to 0/20 at progress 0.43. So the wider array is rejected, and the iteration 1 sensor layout is restored: x = +0.024, +0.012, 0, -0.012, -0.024 m, y = 0.05 m, 16 mm footprints. The single change under test is wheel_track, 0.12 to 0.10 m. A narrower track gives a higher turn rate for the same wheel differential (turn rate = wheel speed difference / wheel_track), so the effective steering authority rises by about 20%. Because the aim is to isolate wheel track, the controller is kept identical to iteration 1: base_speed 1.2, kp 2.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.4, weights [2, 1, 0, -1, -2], last_direction line loss. I did not rescale kp for the narrower track, since that would confound the result. The mass (0.5 kg), wheel radius (0.03 m) and body dimensions are also unchanged. Expected result: slalom and s-bend progress rise above 0.18 and 0.83, and line_loss_events on those tracks fall. The oval finish rate should hold at 1.0. The risk is that the higher effective turn gain raises steering_oscillation on the oval, which I will check against the 0.4 threshold in the Builder's feedback rule.
